title: ZeroTetris: A Spacial Feature Similarity-based Sparse MLP Engine for Neural Volume Rendering
problem: Deploying Neural Volume Rendering to existing accelerators is challenging due to its unique and substantial computational requirements. Standard hardware architectures are not optimized for the specific computation patterns of NVR.
motivation: Neural Volume Rendering enables photo-realistic rendering of virtual worlds and has developed rapidly, but its computational demands require specialized hardware solutions.
method: Neural Volume Rendering creates images by sampling points along rays through 3D space, then processing each sample through a neural network. ZeroTetris exploits the fact that nearby samples produce very similar neural features (the network's internal representations), which means many intermediate calculations will output zero. The accelerator detects these zero-output computations before they execute and skips them, reducing power consumption and chip area. Because Neural Volume Rendering inherently samples at nearby locations, this zero-activation pattern is predictable and reliable to exploit.
key_novelty: Skipping zero-output computations in an MLP accelerator by detecting that nearby samples in Neural Volume Rendering produce nearly identical neural features.
contributions: A dedicated hardware accelerator (ZeroTetris) specifically designed for Neural Volume Rendering
Identification and exploitation of spatial feature similarity-based sparsity patterns in NVR models
Energy-efficient sparse MLP computation through selective activation skipping
Superior area and power efficiency compared to existing sparse multiplication and MLP accelerators
primary_theme: Spatial sparsity for neural volume rendering acceleration
